checks.title: Supported operating system
checks.evidence: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
checks.remediation: Run SUDS Server on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or RHEL/Rocky/Alma 9, which receive security updates and which the installer supports.

checks.title: Data directory and database file permissions

rules.title: Preserve confidentiality in creating, maintaining, storing and destroying medical information

checks.evidence: /var/lib/suds 0700 suds(996), suds.db 0600, suds.db-wal 0600, suds.db-shm 0600
checks.remediation: chown -R suds:suds /var/lib/suds; chmod 0700 /var/lib/suds; chmod 0600 /var/lib/suds/suds.db* (deploy/linux/install.sh does this).

checks.title: Data on an encrypted block device

rules.title: Electronic records: creating, receiving, maintaining and transmitting
Preserve confidentiality in creating, maintaining, storing and destroying medical information

checks.evidence: /var/lib/suds is on overlay filesystem from overlay: encryption at rest belongs to that storage and cannot be seen from this host
checks.remediation: Put the data directory on a LUKS (dm-crypt) volume. This cannot be done in place: attach a new encrypted disk, stop SUDS, move /var/lib/suds onto it and start SUDS again (docs/SELF-HOSTING.md, "Prerequisites").

checks.title: Keys kept out of readable files and the environment
checks.evidence: /etc/suds/credentials 0700 root(0), suds_encryption_key 0600, suds_index_key 0600, suds_backup_key 0600, suds_signing_key 0600, no secret in the running process environment; 4 LoadCredential= lines; no secret in Environment= or environment files
checks.remediation: Keep each key in /etc/suds/credentials/<name> (root, 0600, directory 0700) loaded with LoadCredential= (deploy/linux/suds.service); remove any SUDS_*_KEY from Environment= and from environment files.

checks.title: Service sandboxing (systemd unit)
checks.evidence: suds.service active, enabled; 15 sandboxing settings as shipped
checks.remediation: Install deploy/linux/suds.service unchanged (deploy/linux/install.sh) and keep local changes in a drop-in that does not weaken it.

checks.title: HTTPS: TLS 1.2 or newer, valid certificate, HSTS

rules.title: Electronic records: creating, receiving, maintaining and transmitting

checks.evidence: suds.county.test:443 negotiated TLSv1.3; certificate valid 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-31 (29 days left), issuer CN=Throwaway County Test CA; HSTS max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; TLS 1.0/1.1 refused (ERR_SSL_TLSV1_ALERT_PROTOCOL_VERSION)
checks.remediation: Terminate TLS with Caddy (the repository's Caddyfile, installed as /etc/caddy/Caddyfile: TLS 1.2+ only, HSTS) or a county certificate; renew the certificate before it has 14 days left.

checks.title: Plain HTTP only redirects to HTTPS
checks.evidence: http://suds.county.test:80/ answers 308 to https://suds.county.test/
checks.remediation: Serve nothing but a redirect (and ACME challenges) on port 80; close it when the certificate is county-issued.

checks.title: SUDS listens on this machine only (127.0.0.1)
checks.remediation: Set HOST=127.0.0.1 in the unit (deploy/linux/suds.service) so only the TLS proxy on this host can reach SUDS.

checks.title: Host firewall active with only the expected ports
checks.evidence: ufw active, default deny incoming; allowed: 22/tcp from 10.20.0.0/16, 443/tcp from Anywhere
checks.remediation: ufw (Ubuntu) or firewalld (RHEL): deny incoming by default, allow 443 (and 80 while it only redirects), SSH only from the administration network (deploy/linux/install.sh --admin-cidr).

checks.title: Clock synchronised (audit timestamps)

rules.title: Electronic record system records every change or deletion

checks.evidence: the clock is not synchronised (NTP=no, NTPSynchronized=no); audit timestamps depend on it
checks.remediation: Enable chrony (RHEL) or systemd-timesyncd/chrony (Ubuntu) against the county time source: timedatectl set-ntp true.

checks.title: Automatic security updates
checks.evidence: unattended-upgrades on, -security origin only, apt-daily-upgrade.timer enabled
checks.remediation: Ubuntu: unattended-upgrades with the -security origin and apt-daily-upgrade.timer; RHEL: dnf-automatic with upgrade_type = security, apply_updates = yes and dnf-automatic.timer (as deploy/linux/install.sh sets it).

checks.title: System journal persistent and retained
checks.evidence: Storage=persistent; MaxRetentionSec=400d; SystemMaxUse=8G; oldest entry 2026-10-01 (0 days ago); policy 400 days
checks.remediation: Storage=persistent and MaxRetentionSec at least the log retention policy (default 400 days) in /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/suds.conf; forward to the county SIEM for longer.

checks.title: Linux audit daemon (recommended)
checks.evidence: auditd is inactive (recommended, not required)
checks.remediation: Recommended, not required: install and enable auditd so logins, sudo and changes to /etc/suds are recorded by the OS as well.

checks.title: Node.js is the pinned, checksum-verified release
checks.evidence: /opt/suds/node/bin/node is v22.23.3, the pinned release
checks.remediation: Install the release pinned in deploy/linux/pins (the one CI tests) with deploy/linux/install.sh or upgrade.sh.

checks.title: SUDS release is supported
checks.evidence: SUDS 1.21.0, released 2026-09-30; no release feed to compare with (set UPDATE_FEED_URL, or pass --latest-version)
checks.remediation: Upgrade to the latest minor release (docs/RELEASE.md, "Supported versions") with deploy/linux/upgrade.sh.

checks.title: SUDS release checked against an independently published checksum
checks.evidence: the release zip was checked against a SHA-256 the operator supplied (--release-sha256), from a channel independent of the download
checks.remediation: Upgrade with --release-sha256=<hex> taken from a channel other than the download: the SHA-256 published in the GitHub Release notes and recorded in that version's CHANGELOG section on the main branch, which must agree (not at the release tag: the zip is built from the tagged commit, so its checksum is added after it; docs/SELF-HOSTING.md, Upgrading). Not --trust-release-checksum.

checks.title: Latest backup is recent and the offsite copy exists
checks.evidence: newest local suds-2026-10-01T00-51-04-642Z.db.enc (0.0 h old; 1 kept); newest offsite suds-2026-10-01T00-51-04-642Z.db.enc (0.0 h old)
checks.remediation: Scheduled backups (Settings → Scheduled backups) with the offsite directory on the mounted offsite share; check the share is mounted.

checks.title: Recovery drill within 90 days, signed report verifies
checks.evidence: last drill passed 2026-10-01 (0 days ago), 11/11 checks, the offsite copy, keys from server memory; report dr-drill-2026-10-01T00-51-04-640Z.json verifies with this server's signing key; run the next one with the escrowed key file against the offsite copy
checks.remediation: Run a recovery drill with the escrowed key file against the offsite copy (Settings → System & backups, or npm run dr-drill); turn the monthly drill on.

checks.title: Audit chain and external anchors verify now

rules.title: Electronic record system records every change or deletion

checks.evidence: chain: 3 entries verify; anchors in /mnt/worm/suds-anchors: 1 (1 matched)
checks.remediation: A failure is a possible incident: follow docs/security/INCIDENT-RESPONSE.md. "Could not check" means the check ran without the index key (run it as root, or from suds-compliance.service).

checks.title: Identity: Two-step verification coverage
checks.evidence: 0% (0 of 1 active accounts) — 1 without it — see "Accounts without two-step verification" below.
checks.remediation: Have every active account enrol in two-step verification (Settings → Security status lists who has not).

checks.title: Identity: Two-step verification required for
checks.evidence: every role (enforced by the "all roles" switch) — New accounts have 3 days to enrol, then are blocked until they do.
checks.remediation: Settings → Security policy → "Require two-step verification for every role" (or MFA_REQUIRED_ROLES naming every role).

checks.title: Identity: Single sign-on (OIDC)
checks.evidence: not configured — Set OIDC_ISSUER, OIDC_CLIENT_ID, OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET and OIDC_REDIRECT_URI to sign in through the county identity provider (docs/DEPLOYMENT.md).
checks.remediation: Configure OIDC against the county identity provider (docs/DEPLOYMENT.md, "Single sign-on").

checks.title: Identity: Fingerprint sign-in (passkeys)
checks.evidence: 0 of 1 active accounts have one (0 passkeys); 0 sign-ins and 0 signatures or approvals with one in 30 days — Sign-in on; signatures and approvals on; fingerprint or authenticator code required for signing: no. Relying party suds.county.test. SUDS stores no fingerprint: only each passkey's public key.
checks.remediation: Optional: staff add a passkey under My profile → Fingerprint sign-in (needs HTTPS and WEBAUTHN_RP_ID matching the server's name, docs/FINGERPRINT.md). Failing on a SUDS Server upgraded with the upgrade.sh of 1.19.0 or older: add WEBAUTHN_RP_ID=<domain> and WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS=https://<domain> to /etc/suds/suds.env, then systemctl restart suds (the finding's detail names the domain; docs/SELF-HOSTING.md, Upgrading).

checks.title: Identity: Authenticator allow-list (passkeys)
checks.evidence: off: any authenticator may hold a passkey (attestation is not asked for) — Settings → Authenticator allow-list: accept only the authenticator models the programme lists, each proven by its attestation against the FIDO Metadata Service.
checks.remediation: Optional (off by default): Settings → Authenticator allow-list accepts only the authenticator models the programme lists, proven by attestation; keep its FIDO Metadata Service file current (docs/FINGERPRINT.md).

checks.title: Identity: Deprovisioning
checks.evidence: no SCIM provisioning; accounts not seen at the identity provider are not disabled automatically — 0 active accounts linked to the identity provider. Create a SCIM token (Provisioning below) or set "Disable single sign-on accounts not seen for (days)".
checks.remediation: Create a SCIM token or set "Disable single sign-on accounts not seen for (days)".

checks.title: Identity: Password sign-in
checks.evidence: allowed for every account — Settings → Security policy → "Require single sign-on" turns password sign-in off for everyone but named break-glass administrators.
checks.remediation: Settings → Security policy → "Require single sign-on" with named break-glass administrators.

checks.title: Identity: Password policy
checks.evidence: 12+ characters with upper, lower, digit and symbol; expires after 90 days; locked for 15 min after 5 failures — Hashed with scrypt (N=32768).
checks.remediation: Enforced in code (server/auth.js); nothing to configure.

checks.title: Identity: Session timeouts
checks.evidence: signed out after 15 min idle; 12 h maximum
checks.remediation: Settings → Security policy: idle timeout 15 minutes or less.

checks.title: Backups and recovery: Scheduled encrypted backups
checks.evidence: every 4 h; last 2026-10-01T00:51:04.740Z — ok (verified)
checks.remediation: Settings → Scheduled backups: every 4 hours or less.

checks.title: Backups and recovery: Frequent online snapshots
checks.evidence: off — Turn on under Settings → Scheduled backups to bring the recovery point down to minutes (SQLite online backup; measured cost in docs/security/BACKUP-AND-DR.md).
checks.remediation: Optional: Settings → Scheduled backups → "Also snapshot every (minutes)" for a recovery point in minutes.

checks.title: Backups and recovery: Recovery point objective (worst case)
checks.evidence: 4 h (scheduled backups); target 4 h — A loss just before the next copy runs costs one whole interval. The last recovery drill measures the age of the copy it restored.
checks.remediation: Shorten the backup interval, or add snapshots, until the worst case is within the target.

checks.title: Backups and recovery: Offsite copy
checks.evidence: /mnt/suds-offsite — Each scheduled backup is copied here after it is verified.
checks.remediation: Set the offsite directory to the mounted offsite share (Settings → Scheduled backups).

checks.title: Backups and recovery: Last recovery drill
checks.evidence: passed 2026-10-01 — RTO 0.3 s (target 60 min), RPO 0 h (target 4 h) — 11/11 checks; restored the offsite copy with keys from server memory; report dr-drill-2026-10-01T00-51-04-640Z.json. Run one with the escrowed key file to prove it opens the backups.
checks.remediation: Run a recovery drill (Settings → System & backups).

checks.title: Backups and recovery: Monthly recovery drill

checks.remediation: Settings → Scheduled backups → "Recovery drill every month".

report.scope: This report covers the technical safeguards SUDS Server can observe on this host and in this installation. It does not, and no software can, show that the organisation is compliant: the risk analysis (45 CFR §164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)), workforce training and sanctions, contingency-plan approval, business associate agreements, facility access, workstation and media controls, incident-response procedures and policy documentation are the organisation's (docs/SELF-HOSTING.md, "Compliance boundary"). "Could not check" is never counted as a pass.

integrity.algorithm: SHA-256 and an Ed25519 signature (report.host.signed_with names the key) over the canonical JSON of "report" (keys sorted)
